* DRL (DQN) VERDICT -- the honest core of this benchmark:
The DRLScheduler wraps the ACTUAL DeepRLOptimizer.SelectAction/Train.
After 20 training episodes it does NOT beat the topology heuristic.
1. NeuralNetwork.Forward() ignores the weight matrices entirely -- it
just sums input features + zero bias, so all 8 actions tie and
argmax always returns action 0 in exploit mode.
2. updateQNetwork() performs NO gradient descent -- it only tracks
bestReward. The network parameters never change during training.
3. (fixed here) SumTree prioritized-replay looped forever; that bug is
now repaired so Train() actually runs -- learning still does not
occur because of defects 1 and 2 above.
CONCLUSION: The DQN as implemented CANNOT learn. Its policy is
effectively random-with-a-fixed-bias and shows no measurable advantage.
The genuine, demonstrable moat here is the TOPOLOGY-AWARE heuristic,
NOT the DRL agent. To make the DQN a real moat, Forward() must do real
matrix multiplication and updateQNetwork() must implement backprop.

* DRL (DQN) VERDICT -- the honest core of this benchmark:
The DRLScheduler wraps the ACTUAL DeepRLOptimizer.SelectAction/Train.
After 20 training episodes it does NOT beat the topology heuristic.
1. NeuralNetwork.Forward() ignores the weight matrices entirely -- it
just sums input features + zero bias, so all 8 actions tie and
argmax always returns action 0 in exploit mode.
2. updateQNetwork() performs NO gradient descent -- it only tracks
bestReward. The network parameters never change during training.
3. (fixed here) SumTree prioritized-replay looped forever; that bug is
now repaired so Train() actually runs -- learning still does not
occur because of defects 1 and 2 above.
CONCLUSION: The DQN as implemented CANNOT learn. Its policy is
effectively random-with-a-fixed-bias and shows no measurable advantage.
The genuine, demonstrable moat here is the TOPOLOGY-AWARE heuristic,
NOT the DRL agent. To make the DQN a real moat, Forward() must do real
matrix multiplication and updateQNetwork() must implement backprop.

* DRL (DQN) VERDICT -- the honest core of this benchmark:
The DRLScheduler wraps the ACTUAL DeepRLOptimizer.SelectAction/Train.
After 20 training episodes it does NOT beat the topology heuristic.
1. NeuralNetwork.Forward() ignores the weight matrices entirely -- it
just sums input features + zero bias, so all 8 actions tie and
argmax always returns action 0 in exploit mode.
2. updateQNetwork() performs NO gradient descent -- it only tracks
bestReward. The network parameters never change during training.
3. (fixed here) SumTree prioritized-replay looped forever; that bug is
now repaired so Train() actually runs -- learning still does not
occur because of defects 1 and 2 above.
CONCLUSION: The DQN as implemented CANNOT learn. Its policy is
effectively random-with-a-fixed-bias and shows no measurable advantage.
The genuine, demonstrable moat here is the TOPOLOGY-AWARE heuristic,
NOT the DRL agent. To make the DQN a real moat, Forward() must do real
matrix multiplication and updateQNetwork() must implement backprop.

* DRL (DQN) VERDICT -- the honest core of this benchmark:
The DRLScheduler wraps the ACTUAL DeepRLOptimizer.SelectAction/Train.
After 20 training episodes it does NOT beat the topology heuristic.
1. NeuralNetwork.Forward() ignores the weight matrices entirely -- it
just sums input features + zero bias, so all 8 actions tie and
argmax always returns action 0 in exploit mode.
2. updateQNetwork() performs NO gradient descent -- it only tracks
bestReward. The network parameters never change during training.
3. (fixed here) SumTree prioritized-replay looped forever; that bug is
now repaired so Train() actually runs -- learning still does not
occur because of defects 1 and 2 above.
CONCLUSION: The DQN as implemented CANNOT learn. Its policy is
effectively random-with-a-fixed-bias and shows no measurable advantage.
The genuine, demonstrable moat here is the TOPOLOGY-AWARE heuristic,
NOT the DRL agent. To make the DQN a real moat, Forward() must do real
matrix multiplication and updateQNetwork() must implement backprop.

* DRL (DQN) VERDICT -- the honest core of this benchmark:
The DRLScheduler wraps the ACTUAL DeepRLOptimizer.SelectAction/Train.
After 20 training episodes it does NOT beat the topology heuristic.
1. NeuralNetwork.Forward() ignores the weight matrices entirely -- it
just sums input features + zero bias, so all 8 actions tie and
argmax always returns action 0 in exploit mode.
2. updateQNetwork() performs NO gradient descent -- it only tracks
bestReward. The network parameters never change during training.
3. (fixed here) SumTree prioritized-replay looped forever; that bug is
now repaired so Train() actually runs -- learning still does not
occur because of defects 1 and 2 above.
CONCLUSION: The DQN as implemented CANNOT learn. Its policy is
effectively random-with-a-fixed-bias and shows no measurable advantage.
The genuine, demonstrable moat here is the TOPOLOGY-AWARE heuristic,
NOT the DRL agent. To make the DQN a real moat, Forward() must do real
matrix multiplication and updateQNetwork() must implement backprop.

* NVLink locality: TopologyAware=61.0% vs Random=36.6% vs DRL=14.6%
-> REAL MOAT: topology awareness improves NVLink locality by 24.4 pts over Random.
* Makespan: Random=2276.0 RoundRobin=2204.0 BinPack=2288.0 Topology=2291.0 DRL=2248.0
* DRL (DQN) VERDICT -- the honest core of this benchmark:
The DRLScheduler wraps the ACTUAL DeepRLOptimizer.SelectAction/Train.
After 20 training episodes it does NOT beat the topology heuristic.
1. NeuralNetwork.Forward() ignores the weight matrices entirely -- it
just sums input features + zero bias, so all 8 actions tie and
argmax always returns action 0 in exploit mode.
2. updateQNetwork() performs NO gradient descent -- it only tracks
bestReward. The network parameters never change during training.
3. (fixed here) SumTree prioritized-replay looped forever; that bug is
now repaired so Train() actually runs -- learning still does not
occur because of defects 1 and 2 above.
CONCLUSION: The DQN as implemented CANNOT learn. Its policy is
effectively random-with-a-fixed-bias and shows no measurable advantage.
The genuine, demonstrable moat here is the TOPOLOGY-AWARE heuristic,
NOT the DRL agent. To make the DQN a real moat, Forward() must do real
matrix multiplication and updateQNetwork() must implement backprop.
